family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Join a list of strings into a natural-language list with 'and' before the last item. If any item itself contains a comma, use semicolons as the separators instead of commas (to avoid ambiguity), otherwise use commas as normal; the oxford-style separator before 'and' follows the same rule for three or more items.
visible_tests: assert oxford_join_semicolon(['Tokyo, Japan', 'Paris, France']) == 'Tokyo, Japan and Paris, France'
hidden_tests: assert oxford_join_semicolon(['Acme, Inc.', 'Globex', 'Initech, LLC']) == 'Acme, Inc.; Globex; and Initech, LLC'
assert oxford_join_semicolon(['a, b', 'c']) == 'a, b and c'
assert oxford_join_semicolon(['no commas here', 'or here']) == 'no commas here and or here'
assert oxford_join_semicolon(['Smith, John', 'Doe, Jane', 'Roe, Richard']) == 'Smith, John; Doe, Jane; and Roe, Richard'
assert oxford_join_semicolon(['p', 'q', 'r', 's']) == 'p, q, r, and s'
assert oxford_join_semicolon(['comma, inside', 'plain']) == 'comma, inside and plain'
assert oxford_join_semicolon(['only two, with comma', 'second']) == 'only two, with comma and second'
assert oxford_join_semicolon(['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']) == 'a, b, c, and d'
assert oxford_join_semicolon(['x, y', 'z, w', 'v']) == 'x, y; z, w; and v'
assert oxford_join_semicolon(['hello, world', 'foo, bar', 'baz']) == 'hello, world; foo, bar; and baz'

def smart_quotes(s):
    return "“" + s + "”"

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a block of text, prefix every line (split on newline characters) with '> ' to render it as a markdown-style blockquote, then rejoin the lines with newline characters.
hidden_tests: assert block_quote('single line only') == '> single line only'

assert block_quote('multi
line
text
here') == '> multi
> line
> text
> here'

assert block_quote('x
y
z
w') == '> x
> y
> z
> w'
assert block_quote('emoji-free plain text') == '> emoji-free plain text'
reference:
def block_quote(text):
    return "\n".join("> " + line for line in text.split("\n"))

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Draw a simple box of plus-sign corners, dash top and bottom borders, and pipe sides around a single word, with one space of padding on each side of the word. Return the three lines joined by newline characters: top border, then the padded word row, then the same border again.
hidden_tests: assert box_word('word with space') == '+-----------------+\n| word with space |\n+-----------------+'
reference:
def box_word(word):
    top = "+" + "-" * (len(word) + 2) + "+"
    mid = "| " + word + " |"
    return top + "\n" + mid + "\n" + top

spec: Center the given word, surrounded by a single space on each side, within a line of the given total width, padding with the given fill character on both sides. If the width is not greater than the word plus its two surrounding spaces, the padded word (with its single spaces) is returned unchanged.
reference:
def banner_line(word, width, fill):
    return (" " + word + " ").center(width, fill)

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Draw a box of plus-sign corners, dash borders, and pipe sides around a single word, with the given number of padding spaces on each side of the word inside the box. Return the top border, the padded word row, and the bottom border joined by newline characters.
hidden_tests: assert box_word_padded('word with space', 1) == '+-----------------+\n| word with space |\n+-----------------+'
reference:
def box_word_padded(word, pad):
    inner = " " * pad + word + " " * pad
    top = "+" + "-" * len(inner) + "+"
    mid = "|" + inner + "|"
    return top + "\n" + mid + "\n" + top

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Draw a box made entirely of '#' characters around a single word: a top row of '#' characters exactly 4 longer than the word, a middle row of '# ' then the word then ' #', and the same top row repeated at the bottom. Return the three rows joined by newline characters.
hidden_tests: assert double_box_word('word with space') == '###################\n# word with space #\n###################'
reference:
def double_box_word(word):
    top = "#" * (len(word) + 4)
    mid = "# " + word + " #"
    return top + "\n" + mid + "\n" + top

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Build a three-line banner around a single word: a border line made of '=' characters exactly 4 longer than the word, a middle line formatted as '= word =', and the same border line repeated at the bottom. Return the three lines joined by newline characters.
hidden_tests: assert banner_multiline('word with space') == '===================\n= word with space =\n==================='
reference:
def banner_multiline(word):
    border = "=" * (len(word) + 4)
    mid = "= " + word + " ="
    return border + "\n" + mid + "\n" + border

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Draw a single-character-bordered box around a word using only the given character ch for both the border and the sides: the top row is ch repeated (word length plus 4) times, the middle row is ch, a space, the word, a space, then ch, and the bottom row repeats the top row. Return the three rows joined by newline characters.
hidden_tests: assert box_word_char('word with space', '-') == '-------------------\n- word with space -\n-------------------'
reference:
def box_word_char(word, ch):
    top = ch + ch * (len(word) + 2) + ch
    mid = ch + " " + word + " " + ch
    return top + "\n" + mid + "\n" + top

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Build a three-line title banner of the given total width: a border line of '-' characters spanning the full width, a middle line with the word centered using spaces to fill the width, and the same border line repeated at the bottom. Return the three lines joined by newline characters.
reference:
def title_banner(word, width):
    border = "-" * width
    mid = word.center(width)
    return border + "\n" + mid + "\n" + border

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Draw a box around a word with distinct corner, side, and top/bottom border characters: the border rows are the corner character, then the top character repeated (word length plus 2) times, then the corner character again; the middle row is the side character, a space, the word, a space, then the side character. Return the top border, middle row, and bottom border joined by newline characters.
hidden_tests: assert box_with_corners('word with space', '+', '|', '-') == '+-----------------+\n| word with space |\n+-----------------+'
reference:
def box_with_corners(word, corner, side, top):
    border = corner + top * (len(word) + 2) + corner
    mid = side + " " + word + " " + side
    return border + "\n" + mid + "\n" + border
